Definition: to commit adultery (usually of the female, and less often of simple fornication, rarely of involuntary ravishment); figuratively, to commit idolatry (the Jewish people being regarded as the spouse of Jehovah)
BiblicalUsage: Zanah is to commit adultery, and Scripture uses it for the body and for the soul. After Dinah is defiled, Genesis 34:31 asks, "Should he deal with our sister as with an harlot?" Exodus 34:15 warns against covenants with the inhabitants of the land, lest they go a whoring after their gods. Leviticus 17:7 forbids sacrificing "unto devils, after whom they have gone a whoring," and Numbers 15:39 ties the fringes on the garments to remembering the commandments, "that ye seek not after your own heart and your own eyes, after which ye use to go a whoring."
TheologicalSignificance: I believe God chose this word to shock me, because he calls idolatry what it is: unfaithfulness to a husband. I hold that Exodus 34:15 and Leviticus 17:7 are saying the same thing, that worshipping other gods is adultery against the Lord, and that Numbers 15:39 gives me the guard against it, remembering his commandments. My position is that zanah leaves no room for a divided heart.
